rewrite.title: SEC Probes Nvidia’s AI Revenue Accounting
rewrite.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has opened a formal investigation into Nvidia Corp., targeting the company’s accounting for its explosive AI‑related sales. The probe, initiated in the second quarter of 2024, follows anonymous whistle‑blower filings that allege Nvidia may have used aggressive "bill‑and‑hold" tactics to recognize revenue before hardware was actually delivered to customers. 

Nvidia’s latest earnings report showed a staggering $28.3 billion in revenue for the fiscal quarter ending July 28, a 262% increase year‑over‑year, propelling its market value past the $1 trillion mark. While the growth underscores the chipmaker’s dominance in the generative‑AI market, it also raises questions about the sustainability of such rapid expansion and the robustness of its financial reporting. 

If the SEC finds that revenue was prematurely booked, Nvidia could be forced to restate earnings, potentially lowering its earnings‑per‑share guidance and triggering covenant breaches on its $10 billion revolving credit facility. A restatement would likely ripple through the broader AI ecosystem, prompting investors and regulators to scrutinize other high‑growth tech firms that rely on similar accounting treatments. 

Market participants are already factoring in a risk premium; analysts have trimmed price targets by an average of 8% since the news broke. The investigation also puts a spotlight on Nvidia’s supply chain partners, who may face secondary inquiries if the SEC uncovers systemic issues in how AI hardware orders are recorded. 

While the outcome remains uncertain, the probe underscores the tension between rapid innovation and regulatory oversight. Investors will be watching for any SEC filings or corporate disclosures that could signal the scale of any required adjustments, as the chipmaker’s valuation remains highly sensitive to both earnings momentum and compliance risk.
